newsitem.title: USA: Mass. governor vows to veto any land transfer tax.
newsitem.headline: Mass. governor vows to veto any land transfer tax.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. Paul Cellucci on Monday vowed to veto any land transfer tax bills that come to his desk.

"I've noticed that the number of land transfer tax bills pending in the Legislature has doubled in the last three-and-a-half months," Cellucci told reporters at a State House press conference. "This is an idea that seems to be gaining momentum in the Legislature and around the state." There are currently 16 bills on the matter pending.
He told reporters that "I'm here today to tell the Legislature that they can vote for a land tax, but I'm going to veto it."

Cellucci called the land transfer tax "an elitest, exclusionary tax that would prevent middle-class people, like first-time home buyers and senior citizens just about to retire, from being able to buy the house of their dreams."
The 16 bills being the Legislature would impose between 1.0 and 4.0 percent sales tax on home and land buyers throughout the state.

Cellucci said that communities that wish to dedicate funds to particular purposes -- housing, recreation or general government spending -- should either work within their existing budget or propose a more open tax raising measure.
